report.answer_text:
The President’s Daily Brief (PDB) goes to the U.S. president, the vice president, and a small group of senior officials chosen by the president. That list can vary by administration, but it has often included the national security adviser and the secretaries of state and defense. (cia.gov)
Members of Congress do not routinely receive the PDB. It is highly classified, though some historical briefs have been declassified and released to the public. (cia.gov)

quotes.text: The DA also contributes to the President’s Daily Brief (PDB), which is an Intelligence Community daily product overseen by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI). Because information in these two publications is extremely sensitive, they are highly classified and have restricted readership.
